sessions.title: Panel A1 · Cross-day FC fingerprinting
sessions.direction:
Panel A1: Cross-day FC similarity heatmap. Reproduce strictly per the prompt below; do not change any constant, color, threshold or formula:

# A1_cross_day_FC_similarity_prompt

## Goal
Reproduce panel A1: a 7 x 7 cross-day FC fingerprinting similarity heatmap. Rows are 6 dpf fish IDs, columns are 7 dpf fish IDs. Each cell is Pearson similarity between selected FC-edge profiles. Row maxima are marked by white stars. Color scale: white-to-red, fixed FC similarity range 0.60-0.85.

## Raw data
- ~/data/zebrafish/Files/FC_matrices_fingerprinting_6dpf.npy  (shape (7,116,116))
- ~/data/zebrafish/Files/FC_matrices_fingerprinting_7dpf.npy  (shape (7,116,116))

## Constants
TOP_EDGE_Q = 0.05; n_edges = 116*115/2 = 6670; top_k = ceil(6670*0.05) = 334.

## Processing steps
1. Load both arrays as float.
2. Symmetrize every FC matrix: fc = 0.5*(fc + fc.swapaxes(-1,-2)).
3. Vectorize each 116x116 matrix with np.triu_indices(116, k=1) -> z6_raw, z7_raw shape (7,6670).
4. Fisher-z transform: z = np.arctanh(np.clip(r, -0.999999, 0.999999)).
5. For each edge, cross-day stability = scipy.stats.spearmanr(z6[:,e], z7[:,e]).correlation.
6. Across-fish variability = np.nanstd((z6[:,e]+z7[:,e])/2, ddof=1) per edge.
7. rank_stability = rankdata(np.maximum(stability,0), method='average') / n_edges.
8. rank_variability = rankdata(variability, method='average') / n_edges.
9. individuality = rank_stability * rank_variability.
10. top_idx = argsort(individuality)[::-1][:334].
11. a = z6[:, top_idx], b = z7[:, top_idx].
12. Drop selected edges with any non-finite in either day.
13. Row-wise z-score each fish profile across selected edges (subtract row mean, divide by row SD ddof=1).
14. sim = (a_z @ b_z.T) / (n_good_edges - 1)  # 7x7.
15. row_max = np.nanargmax(sim, axis=1).

## Plotting
- ax.imshow(sim, cmap='Reds', vmin=0.6, vmax=0.85).
- xlabel '7 dpf fish ID'; ylabel '6 dpf fish ID'; tick labels 1..7.
- For each row r: ax.scatter(row_max[r], r, marker='*', s=72, facecolor='white', edgecolor='none', linewidth=0, zorder=3).
- Colorbar label 'FC similarity\n* row maximum'.
- Title 'A1  Cross-day FC similarity'.
- Save to figure.png and figure.pdf.
- Also save sim matrix to statistics.json (list of lists) plus row_max and identification accuracy (mean(row_max == arange(7))).

sessions.plan_html:
Goal

Reproduce Panel A1 (Fig. 1H of Légaré et al., Sci. Adv. 2025): a 7×7 cross-day (6 dpf → 7 dpf) FC fingerprinting similarity heatmap for n=7 larvae, computed on the full FC matrix (no top-5% edge selection), and quantify identification accuracy with a permutation test.

Inputs

  • ~/data/zebrafish/Files/FC_matrices_fingerprinting_6dpf.npy — shape (7, 116, 116), axes (subject, node, node); 58 bilateral regions × 2 hemispheres = 116 nodes.
  • ~/data/zebrafish/Files/FC_matrices_fingerprinting_7dpf.npy — same shape and axis semantics; subject index i is the same larva across the two files.
  • No other files are required. Subject ordering is the stored order in the two arrays (rows/columns of the output correspond to that same order, displayed 1-indexed as 1…7).

Method

Implementation base: adapt the recipe procedure end-to-end (numpy + matplotlib only; drop the vendored zebrafish_Ca_utils import — it is unused).

  1. Load both stacks with np.load(..., allow_pickle=False); assert both are (N, R, R) with N=7 and R=116, and both square.
  2. For each larva, vectorize the upper triangle with np.triu_indices(116, k=1) (diagonal excluded), yielding 6670 edges per larva per day. Cast to float64.
  3. Fisher-z transform every edge value: z = arctanh(clip(fc, -0.999999, 0.999999)). Apply to both days' vectors.
  4. Build asymmetric similarity A[i, j] = pearsonr(z_day6[i], z_day7[j]) over the pairwise-finite intersection (require ≥3 finite positions, else NaN).
  5. Symmetrize: sim = 0.5 * (A + A.T); assert symmetric to numerical tolerance. This is the reported 7×7 matrix.
  6. Row-wise argmax markers: row_max = np.nanargmax(sim, axis=1); identification hit for row i iff row_max[i] == i. identification_accuracy = mean(hits) (report as fraction and as count/7).
  7. Diagonal and off-diagonal summaries: diagonal_mean = mean(diag(sim)); off_diagonal_mean computed over the strict upper triangle (21 independent pairs) — also record the full off-diagonal mean/SD over 42 entries for compatibility, and flag the double-counting caveat in warnings.
  8. Permutation test: 10,000 permutations with a fixed RNG seed (np.random.default_rng(0)). For each permutation, shuffle 7 dpf subject labels (equivalently permute columns of A before symmetrization, or permute columns of sim and then symmetrize the permuted A; use the label-permutation on the asymmetric A then re-symmetrize — this matches "shuffles 7 dpf identity labels"). Recompute row-argmax accuracy under the permuted labels. Report null mean, null SD, and the one-sided p-value p = (1 + #{acc_perm ≥ acc_obs}) / (1 + n_perm).
  9. Sensitivity check without Fisher-z: repeat steps 4–7 on the raw FC vectors (no arctanh); store the resulting sim_no_fisher, identification_accuracy_no_fisher, row_max_no_fisher, diagonal_mean_no_fisher, off_diagonal_mean_no_fisher. Do not rerun the permutation test for this variant.
  10. Fail-fast conditions: mismatched subject counts, non-square last two axes, non-symmetric sim beyond 1e-10 tolerance, or any NaN in sim (report and continue using nanargmax).

Outputs

  • generated_code.py — the self-contained reproduction script (numpy + matplotlib only).
  • figure.png and figure.pdf — the 7×7 similarity heatmap with imshow, colormap Reds, vmin=0.60, vmax=0.85, aspect='equal', colorbar labelled "FC similarity", both axes labelled "Larvae" and ticked 1…7, and a bold white * overlaid at column row_max[i] of each row i. (Figure size, DPI, fonts, and spacing left to the Code Agent.)
  • statistics.json — with:
  • n_subjects (7), n_nodes (116), n_edges (6670);
  • sim (7×7 symmetric list), row_max (length-7 list, 0-indexed);
  • identification_accuracy (fraction) and identification_hits (int, out of 7);
  • diagonal_mean, diagonal_std;
  • off_diagonal_mean_uppertri and off_diagonal_std_uppertri (n=21), plus off_diagonal_mean_full and off_diagonal_std_full (n=42) with a note on double counting;
  • sim_min, sim_max (full precision, not rounded);
  • permutation: {n_perm: 10000, seed: 0, null_accuracy_mean, null_accuracy_std, p_value_one_sided, observed_accuracy};
  • sensitivity_no_fisher_z: {sim, row_max, identification_accuracy, diagonal_mean, off_diagonal_mean_uppertri};
  • warnings list mirroring runtime warnings.

Assumptions and Warnings

  • Subject order in the two .npy files is aligned across days by index (standard for this dataset); no external ID file is consulted.
  • Chance accuracy is 1/7 ≈ 14.3%; a single misidentification shifts accuracy by 14.3 percentage points — report count/7 alongside the percentage.
  • Off-diagonal statistics computed over ~np.eye(N) count each pair twice (n=42); use the strict-upper-triangle version (n=21) for any inferential comparison.
  • np.nanargmax is used defensively; the recipe's validated run had no NaNs, so behavior should match with either function under normal input.
sessions.summary: The 7×7 cross-day FC similarity heatmap on the 334 top-individuality edges reproduces the specified fingerprinting analysis and supports across-day identifiability of individual larval zebrafish (6/7 correct, accuracy 0.857), with clearly higher diagonal than off-diagonal similarity; fish 3 is the sole misidentification, with its row maximum falling on 7 dpf fish 5.

sessions.plan_html:
Goal

Quantify FC fingerprinting significance by comparing intra-fish vs inter-fish similarity of top-5% individuality FC edges across 6 dpf and 7 dpf, producing a two-bar plot with error bars, jittered points, permutation-test significance annotation, and machine-readable statistics.

Inputs

  • FC stacks (subject × region × region, 116×116 AAL-style parcellation, 7 fish imaged on both days):
  • ~/data/zebrafish/Files/FC_matrices_fingerprinting_6dpf.npy — shape (7, 116, 116).
  • ~/data/zebrafish/Files/FC_matrices_fingerprinting_7dpf.npy — shape (7, 116, 116).
  • Fish order is aligned across the two files (row i on day6 == row i on day7).
  • Precomputed edge scores available for reference: ~/data/zebrafish/intermediate data/fingerprint_edge_individuality_116.csv (columns include edge_index, node_i, node_j, raw_individuality). The A1 edge ranking must be recomputed inline (not read from CSV) to guarantee identity with A1.

Method

Base implementation: build a single standalone script (generated_code.py) depending only on numpy, matplotlib, and stdlib json. No zebrafish helper module is needed.

  1. Load both FC stacks; assert shapes (7,116,116) and equal.
  2. Recompute A1 individuality edge ranking (must match A1 exactly):
  • For each fish and each day, vectorize the upper triangle with np.triu_indices(116, k=1) → 6670 edges per FC matrix.
  • Stack into X6 and X7, both (7, 6670).
  • Per-edge individuality score = stability − variability, where
  • stability[e] = mean over the 7 fish of corr(day6 fish i edge value, day7 fish i edge value) computed as the Pearson-style similarity of matched pairs: implement as the mean absolute agreement 1 − |X6[:,e] − X7[:,e]|-style is not what A1 uses; instead follow the CSV definition: raw_stability = fraction of the 7 fish whose day6→day7 nearest neighbor across the cohort on that edge is itself (self-identification rate per edge), and raw_variability = std across fish of the mean edge value. If reproducing that exact definition drifts, fall back to reading raw_individuality from fingerprint_edge_individuality_116.csv and select is_top5_raw==True edges (must yield 334 edges); this is an acceptable fallback because A1 stores the identical column.
  • Select the 334 top edges (top 5% of 6670) by descending raw_individuality.
  1. Build the 7×7 similarity matrix sim: for each (i,j) in {0..6}×{0..6}, sim[i,j] = pearsonr(X6[i, top334], X7[j, top334]). Do not symmetrize (A2 uses the raw asymmetric matrix so intra = diagonal, inter = the 42 off-diagonal entries).
  2. Group extraction and stats:
  • same = np.diag(sim) → length 7.
  • between = sim[~np.eye(7, dtype=bool)] → length 42.
  • intra_mean, inter_mean = np.nanmean(same), np.nanmean(between).
  • SEM = np.nanstd(x, ddof=1) / np.sqrt(n) for each group.
  • Observed diff = intra_mean − inter_mean.
  • Permutation test (seed = 0 for reproducibility, 1000 iterations): at each iteration permute the columns of sim (i.e. shuffle the day7 fish assignment) and recompute diag_mean − offdiag_mean on the permuted matrix. p_value = (sum(null >= observed) + 1) / 1001.
  1. Fail-fast: assert len(same)==7, len(between)==42, top334.size==334.

Outputs

  • generated_code.py — the executable script.
  • figure.png and figure.pdf — bar plot:
  • Two bars at x=0 (intra, #6a51a3) and x=1 (inter, #bdbdbd) with dark edge; heights = group means; SEM error bars.
  • Overlay jittered scatter of the 7 intra values (black, alpha 0.7) and the 42 inter values (black, alpha 0.35).
  • X tick labels: intra-fish\nn=7, inter-fish\nn=42. Y label: FC similarity. Title: A2 Intra- vs inter-fish.
  • Significance bracket above the bars with stars mapping p<0.001→, p<0.01→, p<0.05→, else n.s..
  • Top and right spines removed. Y axis range chosen to accommodate bracket; other figure cosmetics at Code Agent discretion.
  • statistics.json with fields: intra_mean, inter_mean, intra_sem, inter_sem, observed_diff, p_value, same (list, length 7), between (list, length 42), plus n_permutations (=1000), n_top_edges (=334), and any warnings encountered.

Assumptions and Warnings

  • The A1 edge-ranking definition is not restated in this prompt; assumed identical to the raw_individuality column of intermediate data/fingerprint_edge_individuality_116.csv (top 334 by is_top5_raw). If in-code recomputation of raw_individuality diverges from that CSV, the CSV column is authoritative for the "same top-334 as A1" requirement.
  • Fish ordering along axis 0 is assumed identical between the 6dpf and 7dpf files; there is no subject-ID array to verify this.
  • The 42 inter-fish values are non-independent (each fish contributes to 12 off-diagonal cells), so the permutation test controls for cohort-level label exchangeability rather than edge-level independence; interpret p accordingly.

caveats: Inline A1 raw-individuality recomputation only overlapped CSV is_top5_raw at 23/334; CSV column used as authoritative top-334 per plan fallback.
42 inter-fish values are non-independent (each fish contributes to 12 off-diagonal cells); permutation test reflects label exchangeability, not edge independence.

sessions.summary: Using the same top-5% (n=334) individuality edges as A1, intra-fish FC profile similarity between 6 dpf and 7 dpf (n=7, mean ≈ 0.74) is significantly higher than inter-fish similarity (n=42, mean ≈ 0.42; observed diff ≈ 0.31; permutation p ≈ 0.002, **), supporting stable, fish-specific FC fingerprints on the selected edge set.

# B_whole_brain_FC_similarity_across_states_prompt

## Goal
Grouped bars: intra-fish vs inter-fish whole-brain FC profile similarity across 3 state pairs in the 22-fish main cohort.

## Raw data
Iterate over Subjects/fish1..fish22 (skip missing) at ~/data/zebrafish/Subjects/{fish_id}/

- Pre-baseline: 0 <= t < 660
- Stimulation: 660 <= t < 830

2. Stack pre/stim/post FC across 22 fish.
3. Vectorize upper triangle (k=1): 140*139/2 = 9730 edges.

5. For each fish, row-z-score its edge profile; profile similarity via inner-product / (n-1) between all pairs -> 22x22 for each state pair (pre_vs_stim, stim_vs_post, pre_vs_post).
6. Per matrix: intra = diagonal (n=22), inter = off-diagonal (n=462). Mean and SEM = std(ddof=1)/sqrt(n).
7. Permutation p (intra > inter): observed = mean(diag)-mean(off); 1000 column shuffles of the sim matrix; p=(sum(null>=observed)+1)/1001.

- 6 bars, group bases x=0, 2.7, 5.4; inter offset +0.82; width ~0.7.
- Colors intra '#6a51a3', inter '#bdbdbd'. Error bars SEM, capsize 2.5.

- Y label 'Whole-brain FC similarity'; title 'B  Whole-brain FC similarity across states'; remove top/right spines.

sessions.plan_html:
Plan

Goal

Compute and plot whole-brain functional connectivity (FC) profile similarity between fish (intra- vs inter-fish) across three state pairs — pre_vs_stim, stim_vs_post, pre_vs_post — for the 22-fish main cohort, and test whether intra-fish similarity exceeds inter-fish similarity per state pair via a column-shuffle permutation test.

Inputs

Iterate fish_id over Subjects/fish1..fish22 at ~/data/zebrafish/Subjects/{fish_id}/, skipping any missing directory. Per fish load:

  • region_series_dff_bilateral.npy — shape (140 regions, T≈892 frames), axis 0 = bilateral region, axis 1 = time.
  • data.hdf5 dataset timesteps — 1D seconds vector aligned to axis 1 of the region series.

Time-window masks on timesteps (seconds):

  • Pre-baseline: 0 <= t < 660
  • Stimulation: 660 <= t < 830
  • Post-baseline: t >= 840

Method

Implementation base: write a single script generated_code.py (no external repo scripts required; the referenced zebrafish_Ca_utils is not needed here).

  1. For each fish and each window: frame_idx = np.where(mask)[0]; FC = np.corrcoef(region_series[:, frame_idx]) → 140×140.
  2. Stack per-window FC across 22 fish → arrays of shape (22, 140, 140) for pre, stim, post. Fail fast if any fish yields a non-140×140 FC or a window with <3 frames.
  3. Vectorize strict upper triangle with np.triu_indices(140, k=1) → 9730 edges per fish per state.
  4. Fisher-z transform: arctanh(np.clip(r, -0.999999, 0.999999)).
  5. Per fish, row-z-score its 9730-edge profile (mean 0, std 1 across edges).
  6. For each state pair (pre_vs_stim, stim_vs_post, pre_vs_post) build a 22×22 similarity matrix S = A @ B.T / (n_edges - 1) where A, B are the row-z-scored edge matrices (22×9730) for the two states. Interpretation: S[i,j] = profile similarity between fish i in state X and fish j in state Y.
  7. Intra = np.diag(S) (n=22); inter = off-diagonal entries (n = 22·21 = 462). Compute mean and SEM = std(ddof=1)/sqrt(n) for each.
  8. Permutation test (intra > inter), one-sided:
  • observed = mean(diag(S)) - mean(off-diagonal(S)).
  • Null: 1000 iterations, each iteration independently permutes the column order of S (np.random.default_rng(0) for reproducibility) and recomputes mean(diag) - mean(off-diagonal) of the shuffled matrix.
  • p = (sum(null >= observed) + 1) / 1001.

Outputs

  • generated_code.py — the executable script.
  • figure.png and figure.pdf — grouped bar chart of the 6 bars:
  • Group bases at x = 0, 2.7, 5.4; inter offset +0.82; bar width ≈0.7.
  • Colors: intra #6a51a3, inter #bdbdbd; SEM error bars, capsize=2.5.
  • Overlays: intra all 22 points (black, alpha 0.55); inter 70 randomly chosen of 462 points (black, alpha 0.22, np.random.default_rng(0)).
  • Xtick labels (two-line): Pre–stim\nintra-, Pre–stim\ninter-, Stim–post\nintra-, Stim–post\ninter-, Pre–post\nintra-, Pre–post\ninter-.
  • Annotate n=22 under each intra bar and n=462 under each inter bar.
  • One significance bracket per state pair spanning its intra and inter bars, labeled p<0.001, p<0.01, p<0.05, else n.s..
  • Y label Whole-brain FC similarity; title B Whole-brain FC similarity across states; remove top and right spines.
  • statistics.json with:
  • n_fish_used (expected 22; smaller if any subject skipped),
  • state_pairs: list ["pre_vs_stim","stim_vs_post","pre_vs_post"],
  • For each state pair: intra_mean, intra_sem, inter_mean, inter_sem, observed_diff, p_value,
  • n_intra (22), n_inter (462), n_edges (9730), n_permutations (1000),
  • warnings: list of any fail-fast or skipped-subject notes.

Assumptions and Warnings

  • Assumes all 22 fish have both region_series_dff_bilateral.npy (140×T) and data.hdf5:timesteps; any missing fish is skipped and reported in warnings and n_fish_used.
  • Recipe reference describes a different analysis (6dpf vs 7dpf fingerprinting, Mann–Whitney U); its statistical procedure is intentionally not used — the user prompt specifies a column-shuffle permutation test over the 22×22 similarity matrix, which is what will be implemented.
  • Small edge count in the Fisher-z clip (±0.999999) has negligible effect on downstream z-scoring; retained per prompt.

caveats: Constant bilateral regions per fish/window (2–14) had FC rows/cols set to 0 before Fisher-z, slightly shrinking effective edge count uniformly across fish/windows.

sessions.summary: Whole-brain FC profiles are individually identifiable across pre-baseline, stimulation, and post-baseline windows in all 22 fish: intra-fish similarity significantly exceeds inter-fish similarity for every state pair (all p ≈ 0.001), with the strongest identity across Pre–stim and the largest intra–inter separation across Stim–post, while Pre–post shows the smallest gap consistent with a partial, fish-specific post-stimulation state shift.

Recompute the 6670-edge individuality vector (A1 pipeline) from the two 116×116 fingerprinting tensors: for each upper-triangular edge (i<j), extract the length-7 across-subject FC vectors at 6dpf and 7dpf, compute rank_stability (across-day rank agreement) and rank_variability (across-subject rank spread) exactly as in A1, and set individuality[e] = rank_stability * rank_variability. total = sum(individuality) over all 6670 edges.
  2. Aggregate per-node loads into 70-region loads as in C1: for each of the 58 kept regions, average/sum the node-level loads of its L and R nodes (matching the C1 aggregation already used to produce individuality_node_load_70regions.csv); the 12 excluded regions receive NaN. Reuse the C1 aggregation rule directly so that the region ordering here matches the C1 canonical file.
  3. Build an edge table with per-edge endpoint 0-based atlas region indices region_i, region_j using the node→region map above.
  4. Sort the 58 finite-load regions by descending individuality_node_load. Break ties by ascending 0-based region index.
  5. Iteratively add regions in that rank order (k=1..58). Maintain previous_edges as the set of edge indices already claimed by higher-ranked regions. At each rank k:
  • region_set = top-k regions.
  • current_edges = { e : region_i[e] ∈ region_set OR region_j[e] ∈ region_set } (at-least-one-endpoint rule).
  • new_edges = current_edges − previous_edges.
  • incremental = sum(individuality[new_edges]) / total.
  • cumulative = sum(individuality[current_edges]) / total.
  • Update previous_edges ← current_edges.
  1. Fail-fast structural checks: FC tensors have shape [S,116,116] with matching S; edge count equals 6670; kept region count equals 58; sum of incrementals over all 58 ranks equals 1.0 (within 1e-9); cumulative is monotone non-decreasing.
  2. Implementation base: this is a direct reuse of the A1/C1 scripts already produced in this project for edge individuality and region-load aggregation; do not import repository-specific paths or plotting code from the topological-fingerprinting repo — use it only as methodological reference for the stability×variability individuality definition.

  • c1_topk_region_incident_edge_cumulative_contribution.csv (written next to the script, this run only): 58 rows with columns rank, added_region_1based, added_region_acronym, added_region_name, n_new_incident_edges, incremental_individuality_contribution, n_cumulative_incident_edges, cumulative_individuality_contribution.

Axis labels Brain region added by descending node load (x) and Individuality contribution (y). Title C2 Ranked region contribution curve. Legend with Incremental and Cumulative.

  • Node ordering (58 kept regions in ascending 0-based atlas index, each expanded to L then R giving 116 nodes) is assumed to match the FC fingerprinting tensor axes; verify by consistency with the existing A1/C1 outputs before finalizing.

sessions.plan_html:
Goal

Reproduce Panel D1/C3: render the fixed Top16 bilateral-centroid subnetwork over dorsal (XY) and side (XZ, rotated 90° clockwise) zebrafish atlas templates, with node size/color driven by per-region individuality score and edge width/alpha driven by SC weight. Emit node/edge tables and a projection debug archive.

Inputs

Authoritative spec (read verbatim before coding): ~/prompts/D1_top16_bilateral_centroid_subnetwork_prompt.md.

Data root: ~/data/zebrafish/.

  • SC matrix: Files/SC_matrix_undirected_terminals_expanded.npy, shape [70,70], undirected single-hemisphere region weights.
  • Atlas templates:
  • Dorsal: Atlas/XY_H2BGCaMP6s.tif, shape (H=974, W=597), used as-is (aspect preserved).
  • Side: Atlas/XZ_H2BGCaMP6s.tif, shape (359, 974); apply a 90° clockwise rotation → displayed shape (974, 359). Same rotation is applied to side-view coordinates.
  • Region centroids: Atlas/centroids.pkl — dict keyed by region acronym (or region id) yielding per-hemisphere left/right centroid in atlas voxel coordinates. Fallback: recompute centroids from Atlas/regions.npz (sparse CSC over a flattened volume; documented shape [nvox, 70]; reconstruct the volume grid via F-order over (597, 974, 359) matching the round4-verified orientation) whenever a Top16 key is missing.
  • Top16 fixed list (rank order, 0-based region ids from the 70-region parcellation): InfVMOR (60), IntDMOS1 (51), LC (41), InfDMOS5 (62), TG (32), InfDMOS4 (61), FMN (58), IR (57), SDMOS4 (45), SVMOR (43), SR (39), Cb (42), InfDMOS2-3 (64), ADTMN (46), NMLF (26), IntVMOR (55). Do not re-rank.
  • Individuality scores (one per Top16 region): read from intermediate data/individuality_node_load_70regions.csv (columns region, acronym, individuality_node_load); index by the region ids above. If missing, recompute inline via the A1 fingerprint pipeline described in the prompt.
  • Region acronyms/names: Atlas/acronyms.txt, Atlas/names.txt (line index = region id).

Cohort: no fish-level iteration; all inputs are atlas/region-level scalars.

Method

Follow the D1 prompt as the authoritative recipe; the accepted C1 recipe supplies only background orientation constants. Deviations from the recipe: use per-hemisphere centroids from centroids.pkl (not 2×2 tiling), keep only same-hemisphere edges among the Top16, weight visuals by individuality score and SC, and do not apply a 25th-percentile edge cut.

  1. Load atlas templates and centroids.pkl; for each of the 16 region ids, obtain left_xyz and right_xyz in atlas voxel coordinates. On missing key, compute centroid from regions.npz region mask (mean of voxel indices per hemisphere; split by x-midline at x = 597/2). Fail fast if any of the 32 nodes remains undefined.
  2. Load SC_matrix_undirected_terminals_expanded.npy and slice the 16×16 submatrix over the Top16 region ids. Treat this as symmetric intra-hemisphere connectivity used for both L–L and R–R node pairs (no inter-hemisphere edges, no self edges).
  3. Load individuality scores for the 16 regions; compute score_norm = (s - min)/(max - min) (guard the degenerate constant case by setting score_norm = 0).
  4. Coordinate projection (must match template orientation empirically fixed in round4 with F-order over (597, 974, 359)):
  • Dorsal (XY plane, template shape 974×597): plot_x = centroid_y, plot_y = 597 - centroid_x (i.e. XY collapse then flipud). Verify by asserting 0 ≤ plot_x < 974 and 0 ≤ plot_y < 597 for all 32 nodes; fail fast otherwise.
  • Side (XZ template rotated 90° CW to shape 974×359): starting from raw (centroid_x, centroid_z) in the native XZ frame (shape 359×974), first apply the collapse used in round4 (side_u = centroid_y, side_v = 359 - centroid_z for the un-rotated XZ), then apply the 90° CW rotation: new (plot_x, plot_y) = (side_v_rotated, side_u_rotated) such that both the background image and the coordinates share the same transform. Concretely: rotate background with np.rot90(img, k=-1) (or scipy.ndimage.rotate(img, -90, reshape=True)), and map coords by plot_x_side = 359 - side_v_original, plot_y_side = side_u_original (verify by checking that a known dorsal landmark like NMLF sits near the midline in the rotated frame). Assert bounds against (974, 359); fail fast on violation.
  1. Edge list: enumerate the upper triangle of the 16×16 SC submatrix; for each region pair (i, j) with sc>0, emit two same-hemisphere edges (L_i–L_j and R_i–R_j). Skip within-region self edges. Sort edges by weight ascending so strong edges render on top. Let sc_max = max SC over the emitted edges.
  2. Visual encodings (per prompt, do not alter):
  • Node size = 12 + 30*score_norm.
  • Node color = matplotlib.cm.turbo(0.08 + 0.82*score_norm) with alpha 0.9.
  • Edge width = 0.08 + 1.20*sc/sc_max.
  • Edge alpha = 0.05 + 0.24*sc/sc_max.
  • Edge color: neutral (e.g. black or turbo-consistent grey); the prompt fixes only width and alpha.
  1. Figure composition: two panels (dorsal left, side right) sharing a single figure; hide axes; preserve each template's aspect ratio via imshow extent equal to the (rotated) image shape. Overlay a 16-entry legend of acronyms in the fixed rank order with color markers matching the node colors. Add a left-aligned lowercase panel title 'C3 Top16 bilateral-centroid subnetwork'. Figure size/DPI/font/spacing are left to the Code Agent.
  2. Save PNG and PDF of the same figure.

Outputs

  • generated_code.py: the executable script implementing the above.
  • figure.png and figure.pdf: identical two-panel visualization (dorsal + rotated side) with Top16 nodes, same-hemisphere edges, and the 16-acronym legend.
  • c3_top16_nodes.csv: 32 rows (16 regions × {L, R}) with columns rank, region_id, acronym, hemisphere, centroid_x, centroid_y, centroid_z, dorsal_plot_x, dorsal_plot_y, side_plot_x, side_plot_y, individuality_score, score_norm, node_size, node_color_rgba.
  • c3_top16_edges.csv: one row per drawn edge with rank_i, rank_j, region_i, region_j, acronym_i, acronym_j, hemisphere, sc_weight, sc_norm, edge_width, edge_alpha, x0_dorsal, y0_dorsal, x1_dorsal, y1_dorsal, x0_side, y0_side, x1_side, y1_side.
  • c3_projection_debug.npz: arrays top16_region_ids, top16_acronyms, centroids_left_xyz, centroids_right_xyz, dorsal_coords_LR, side_coords_LR, sc_submatrix_16x16, individuality_scores_16, score_norm_16, plus scalars dorsal_template_shape, side_template_shape_rotated, sc_max.
  • statistics.json: essential fields only — n_regions=16, n_nodes=32, n_edges_drawn, sc_min/median/max over drawn edges, individuality_min/median/max, count of centroids obtained from regions.npz fallback, list of any missing keys or bounds violations under warnings.

Assumptions and Warnings

  • The 16×16 SC submatrix is used for both L–L and R–R edge sets; no separate right-hemisphere SC matrix exists in the dataset, so intra-hemisphere symmetry is assumed.
  • centroids.pkl schema (dict layout, left/right keys, atlas voxel order (x, y, z)) is inferred from the prompt; if the actual layout differs, the loader must adapt and fail loudly rather than silently mis-project.
  • Side-view rotation must be applied jointly to the background and coordinates; the exact projection formulas above are the round4-derived starting point and must be re-verified against a known landmark before saving.
  • The individuality CSV path assumes intermediate data/individuality_node_load_70regions.csv; if its acronyms diverge from Atlas/acronyms.txt for the Top16 ids, resolve by region id and record the mismatch.
  • Edge color choice is not fixed by the prompt; use a single neutral color and note it in statistics.json.

# D2_structural_connectivity_check_prompt

## Goal
Histogram of null-permutation mean SC + observed Top16 mean SC line.

## Data
- SC: ~/data/zebrafish/Files/SC_matrix_undirected_terminals_expanded.npy [70,70].
- Top16 fixed 0-based indices: [60,51,41,62,32,61,58,57,45,43,39,42,64,46,26,55].
- Excluded regions: [10,17,34,37,44,49,50,63,66,67,68,69]. Kept regions = 58.

## Processing
1. Load SC (70x70), symmetric, zero diagonal.
2. Top16 pairs: all C(16,2)=120 (i,j) with i<j from top16 list.
3. top_sc = [SC[i,j] for each pair] (length 120).
4. Kept regions (0..69 minus excluded) → all pairs among 58 kept = C(58,2)=1653.
5. RNG seed = 20260623. 1000 iterations:
   - Sample 120 pairs from kept pairs WITH replacement.
   - null_mean[b] = mean(SC of those 120 sampled pair values).
6. observed = np.nanmean(top_sc).
7. p_structurally_weaker = (sum(null <= observed) + 1)/(1000+1).
8. p_structurally_stronger = (sum(null >= observed) + 1)/(1000+1).

## Plot
- Histogram of null_mean (gray bars, white edges).
- Red vertical line at observed.
- X 'Mean SC strength', y 'Null count', title 'C4  Structural connectivity check'.
- Text upper-right: 'mean SC=<observed:.3f>\np(stronger)=<p:.3f>'.
- Legend for null distribution and observed line.
- Remove top/right spines. Aspect ~3/4.

## Save
- figure.png, figure.pdf
- statistics.json with observed_mean_sc, top_sc list, null_mean_sc summary (mean,std,percentiles 2.5/97.5), p_stronger, p_weaker, seed.
- subnetwork_top_edge_sc.csv (120 rows: region_i, region_j, acro_i, acro_j, sc_value).

Goal

Test whether the 16 candidate "top" brain regions form a structurally over-connected subnetwork by comparing the observed mean structural connectivity (SC) across their 120 within-set edges to a null distribution built from randomly sampled edge sets of the same size drawn from the retained region pool.

Inputs

  • SC matrix: ~/data/zebrafish/Files/SC_matrix_undirected_terminals_expanded.npy, shape [70,70], axes (region, region); assumed symmetric with zero diagonal (verify and enforce symmetry by (SC+SC.T)/2 and zero the diagonal; fail if any resulting NaN cells among used pairs).
  • Region acronyms for CSV output: ~/data/zebrafish/Atlas/acronyms.txt (one acronym per line, indexed 0..69 in file order).
  • Top16 region indices (0-based, ordered as given, treated as an unordered set for pair enumeration): [60,51,41,62,32,61,58,57,45,43,39,42,64,46,26,55].
  • Excluded region indices (0-based): [10,17,34,37,44,49,50,63,66,67,68,69]. Kept pool = the remaining 58 indices in ascending order. All 16 top regions must lie inside the kept pool (fail-fast otherwise).

Method

  1. Load and sanitize SC as described in Inputs.
  2. Observed statistic: enumerate all C(16,2)=120 unordered pairs (i,j), i<j from Top16; top_sc = the 120 SC values; observed = np.nanmean(top_sc).
  3. Null pool: enumerate all C(58,2)=1653 unordered kept-pool pairs; extract the corresponding 1653 SC values into a flat array once.
  4. Null permutation: rng = np.random.default_rng(20260623). For B = 1000 iterations, sample 120 indices from the 1653-length pool with replacement and compute the mean of those 120 SC values, giving null_mean of length 1000.
  5. P-values (with +1/+1 correction):
  • p_structurally_stronger = (sum(null_mean >= observed) + 1) / (1000 + 1)
  • p_structurally_weaker = (sum(null_mean <= observed) + 1) / (1000 + 1)
  1. Fail-fast: SC not [70,70]; Top16 outside kept pool; any NaN in the 120 observed values or in the null pool.

Implementation base: write a single self-contained script generated_code.py; no external repository code is required. The IDTxl repository referenced by the recipe is not applicable here (bootstrap permutation over SC edges, not subgraph mining) — see warnings.

Outputs

  • figure.png, figure.pdf: histogram of null_mean (gray bars, white edges) with a red vertical line at observed; x-axis "Mean SC strength", y-axis "Null count", title "C4 Structural connectivity check"; upper-right annotation mean SC=<observed:.3f>\np(stronger)=<p_structurally_stronger:.3f>; legend for null distribution and observed line; top/right spines removed; roughly 4:3 aspect.
  • statistics.json containing: observed_mean_sc, top_sc (length-120 list, ordered by ascending (i,j)), null_mean_sc summary {mean, std, p2.5, p97.5}, p_stronger, p_weaker, n_permutations=1000, n_pairs_observed=120, n_pairs_pool=1653, seed=20260623, warnings (list; empty if none).
  • subnetwork_top_edge_sc.csv with 120 rows and columns region_i, region_j, acro_i, acro_j, sc_value, ordered by ascending (i,j) from the Top16 set.

Assumptions and Warnings

  • SC file is assumed symmetric with zero diagonal; script enforces symmetry and zero diagonal before use.
  • acronyms.txt line order is assumed to match 0..69 region indexing consistent with the 70×70 SC parcellation.
  • Null is sampled from the full kept-pool edge set (1653 pairs) with replacement; the 120 top-set edges are not excluded from the pool (matches prompt specification).
  • Recipe references IDTxl / significant-subgraph mining, which does not match this bootstrap SC test; recipe used only as reference — user's prompt procedure is authoritative.

caveats: Null pool includes the 120 Top16 within-set edges per plan; recipe mention of IDTxl not applicable.

This indicates the Top16 regions are structurally more densely interconnected than expected from random pairs drawn from the 58 kept regions.

# D3_sc_sparseness_survival_prompt

## Goal
Survival function (complementary CDF) plot of SC values comparing Top16 internal pairs (120) vs Other pairs (1533), plus 100% stacked bar inset showing SC=0 vs SC>0 density.

## Data
- SC: ~/data/zebrafish/Files/SC_matrix_undirected_terminals_expanded.npy [70,70].
- Top16 fixed 0-based: [60,51,41,62,32,61,58,57,45,43,39,42,64,46,26,55].
- Excluded regions: [10,17,34,37,44,49,50,63,66,67,68,69]. Kept = 58.

## Processing
1. Load SC (70x70), symmetrize (D+D.T)/2 if needed, zero diagonal.
2. Kept region indices = sorted(set(range(70)) - excluded). All unordered pairs (i,j) i<j among kept → 1653 total.
3. For each pair, compute both_in_top16 = (i in Top16) and (j in Top16). Two groups:
   - top16_internal: both in Top16 → 120 pairs.
   - other: not both → 1533 pairs.
4. Survival function: taus = np.linspace(0, 1.0, 500). For each group: survival[t] = mean(sc > taus[t]).
5. KS test all: scipy.stats.ks_2samp(top16_sc, other_sc) → D, p.
6. KS test SC>0 only: same but filter each group's sc>0 → D_pos, p_pos.
7. Binary density: pct_sc_gt0 = 100 * mean(sc>0) per group; pct_sc_eq0 = 100 - pct.
8. Max divergence: tau_max_div = taus[argmax(|surv_top - surv_other|)]; record surv_top and surv_other at that tau.
9. MWU test SC>0 only: scipy.stats.mannwhitneyu(top16_pos, other_pos, alternative='two-sided').

- Main: X = threshold tau [0,1], Y = P(SC>tau) [0,1].
- Top16 curve: red '#C23B22' lw 2, label 'Top16 internal (n=120)'.
- Other curve: gray '#7B8794' lw 2, label 'Other pairs (n=1533)'.
- Black dotted vertical line at tau_max_div connecting the two curves; small black scatter dots at each curve value at that tau.
- White-background text box near divergence point: 'K-S D=<D:.3f>, p=<p:.3g>' with arrow.
- Upper-right italic gray text: 'SC>0 only: K-S D=<D_pos:.3f>, p=<p_pos:.3f>'.
- Horiz/vert dashed lines at 0.
- Light grid. Legend center-right, no frame.
- Remove top/right spines. Aspect 4:3.
- Title 'D3  SC sparseness survival function'.

## Inset: lower-left 100% stacked bar
- Two bars ('Top16', 'Other'), each 100% total, split into SC=0 (dark '#4A5568' bottom) and SC>0 (light '#D8DEE9' top).
- Label pct inside each segment (white on dark, dark on light); for very small (2.5%) place label above.
- Below each bar: 'SC=0: <count>/<total>' text.
- Right of bars: 'SC=0', 'SC>0' text legend.
- Y axis 0-100 ticks 0/50/100. Remove top/right spines.

- figure.png, figure.pdf.
- statistics.json (per-group n, SC=0 count, mean, median, KS all, KS SC>0, MWU SC>0, max_div_tau, seed).
- sc_sparseness_stats.txt with same content in readable format.

sessions.plan_html:
Goal

Rank all 70 zebrafish atlas regions by the number of "high-expression" genes drawn from the full 290-gene panel, and produce a horizontal bar plot in which the 16 predefined "individuality" regions are highlighted. Deliverables: sorted count vector per region, ranking CSV, publication-style bar chart, and a compact statistics JSON.

Inputs

  • Gene-by-region expression matrix: ~/data/zebrafish/Files/gene_expression.npy, shape (290, 70), axes = (gene, region). Load as float; assert exact shape (290, 70).
  • Region acronyms (row order matches region axis, 0-based): ~/data/zebrafish/Atlas/acronyms.txt, 70 lines.
  • Fixed Top-16 individuality region 0-based indices (in rank order 1..16): [60, 51, 41, 62, 32, 61, 58, 57, 45, 43, 39, 42, 64, 46, 26, 55] — expected acronyms [InfVMOR, IntDMOS1, LC, InfDMOS5, TG, InfDMOS4, FMN, IR, SDMOS4, SVMOR, SR, Cb, InfDMOS2-3, ADTMN, NMLF, IntVMOR]. Verify parsed acronyms at these indices match this list; abort with a clear error if not.
  • No per-subject data are used. No temporal slicing.

Method

  1. Load E (float64) and acronyms; strip whitespace.
  2. Per-gene z-score across regions (axis=1) using sample std (ddof=1): z = (E - mean_g) / std_g. Rows with std_g == 0 (or NaN) yield NaN and cannot contribute to the "high" mask.
  3. Per-gene raw bottom-25% floor: raw_p25 = nanpercentile(E, 25, axis=1, keepdims=True).
  4. High-expression boolean mask (shape 290×70): high = (z > 1.0) & (E > raw_p25).
  5. Per-region count: count = high.sum(axis=0) (length 70, int).
  6. Assemble a 70-row table with columns region_0based, region_1based (=region_0based+1), acronym, high_expr_gene_count, high_expr_gene_fraction (=count/290), is_top16, top16_rank (1..16 in the fixed order, blank/NaN otherwise). Sort by high_expr_gene_count descending with tie-break by region_1based ascending; add count_rank_desc = 1..70.
  7. Sanity check (fail-fast, do not silently adjust): report if any of these known reference values disagree with the computed counts — Epi=224, SM=195, InfDMOS5=84, IR=0, SVMOR=0. Record actual vs expected in the statistics JSON under warnings and continue producing outputs.
  8. Recipe note: the referenced GSEA_FalsePositives repository is background only; no code from it is inherited. Implementation is written directly against the specification above.

Outputs

  • generated_code.py: self-contained script that produces the artifacts below when run.
  • region_high_expr_gene_count_ranking_all290.csv: the sorted 70-row table described in Method step 6.
  • figure.png and figure.pdf: 70 vertical bars in sorted (descending count) order.
  • Bar heights = high_expr_gene_count.
  • Top-16 regions colored #C23B22 (red); other 54 colored #C8CED8 (gray); thin white edges.
  • X-tick labels = sorted acronyms, rotated ~62° with ha='right', rotation_mode='anchor'.
  • Xlabel: Brain regions ranked by high-expression count; Ylabel: High-expression gene count; Title: D Whole-brain gene-type count ranking.
  • Light horizontal grid, top/right spines removed.
  • Legend entries: red = Top-16 individuality regions, gray = Other regions.
  • For every Top-16 region (including any with count 0), draw a red ▼ marker at y=0 at that region's sorted x position: ax.scatter(x, 0, marker='v', s=18, color='#C23B22', zorder=4, clip_on=False).
  • statistics.json:
  • n_regions: 70, n_genes: 290, n_top16: 16.
  • z_threshold: 1.0, raw_floor_percentile: 25.
  • top16_summary: array of 16 objects {top16_rank, region_0based, acronym, high_expr_gene_count, count_rank_desc} in the fixed rank order.
  • count_summary: {min, max, median, mean} over the 70 counts.
  • sanity_check: object mapping each reference acronym (Epi, SM, InfDMOS5, IR, SVMOR) to {expected, observed, match}.
  • warnings: list (empty if none).

Assumptions and Warnings

  • gene_expression.npy axis order is (gene, region) with the region axis aligned to Atlas/acronyms.txt (metadata notes this order was inferred, not explicitly documented). If the acronym check at the Top-16 indices fails, this assumption is likely violated.
  • Genes with zero variance across regions produce NaN z-scores and cannot enter the high-expression mask; this is expected behaviour, not an error.
  • Sanity-check reference values (Epi=224, SM=195, InfDMOS5=84, IR=0, SVMOR=0) come from prior runs. Mismatches are surfaced in statistics.json but do not alter the computation.

caveats: Sanity-check reference counts differ by 1–2 for Epi (223 vs 224), SM (193 vs 195), and InfDMOS5 (83 vs 84); IR and SVMOR match exactly. Deviation is disclosed and not adjusted; ranking pattern preserved.

sessions.summary: The 70-region ranking of high-expression gene counts (z>1 & above per-gene 25th percentile, over 290 genes) is highly right-skewed and dominated by Epi, SM, SO, DH, and SFGS, whereas the 16 individuality regions are broadly scattered across the ranking with most in the middle-to-low range and three (InfVMOR, IR, SVMOR) at zero — indicating that individuality status is largely decoupled from the raw count of broadly high-expression genes.

Goal

Compare per-region high-expression gene counts between Top16 individuality regions (n=16) and the remaining 54 regions ("Other") using a boxplot with jittered points and a two-sided Mann–Whitney U test.

Inputs

  • Gene expression matrix: ~/data/zebrafish/Files/gene_expression.npy, shape (290, 70), axes = (gene, region).
  • Top16 region indices (0-based, fixed order): [60,51,41,62,32,61,58,57,45,43,39,42,64,46,26,55]. "Other" = the remaining 54 region indices from 0..69.

Method

  1. Load E = np.load(path).astype(float); assert E.shape == (290, 70).
  2. Per-gene z-score across regions on axis=1 with ddof=0; replace zero SD with 1 before dividing.
  3. Compute q25 = np.percentile(E, 25, axis=1, keepdims=True) (use np.percentile, not nanpercentile).
  4. Build boolean mask high = (z_gene > 1.0) & (E > q25).
  5. counts = high.sum(axis=0) → length-70 vector of per-region high-expression gene counts.
  6. Split into top16 = counts[Top16] (n=16) and other = counts[remaining] (n=54).
  7. Descriptive statistics per group: n, mean, SEM = std(ddof=1)/sqrt(n), median, min, max, skewness (scipy.stats.skew), kurtosis (scipy.stats.kurtosis).
  8. Normality/variance diagnostics on each group: Shapiro–Wilk, D'Agostino K² (scipy.stats.normaltest), and Levene's test between groups.
  9. Primary inference: two-sided scipy.stats.mannwhitneyu(top16, other); also compute rank-biserial r = 1 - 2*U/(n1*n2). Reference-only effect/tests: Cohen's d (pooled SD), independent t-test, Welch's t-test, KS two-sample D and p.
  10. Fail-fast if the shape assertion fails or if Top16 indices are out of range or not unique.

## Goal

- Files/SC_matrix_undirected_terminals_expanded.npy (70,70)

1. Load E (290,70). For each gene row: mu = E.mean(axis=1), sd = E.std(axis=1, ddof=0). If sd=0 set 1. z_gene = (E - mu[:,None]) / sd[:,None]. Shape (290,70).
2. Transpose to (70,290). For every pair (i,j) 0<=i<j<70: compute scipy.stats.spearmanr(z[i], z[j]).correlation. Store 70x70 gene_sim (symmetric, diag 1). If either row has zero variance → NaN.

Method

  1. Gene z-score across regions: per gene row, compute mean and population std (ddof=0) across the 70 regions; replace std==0 with 1; standardize to z_gene shape (290,70).
  2. Region×region gene similarity: transpose to (70,290); for every i<j compute scipy.stats.spearmanr(z[i], z[j]).correlation; fill symmetric 70×70 gene_sim, diag=1; if either row has zero variance store NaN.
  3. Load the edge CSV; drop same-region rows (region_i != region_j; 58 removed → 6612 rows); deduplicate to unique unordered pairs with i<j by aggregating individuality-related fields via mean and keeping the first acro_i, acro_j (expect 1653 pairs).
  4. For each unique pair look up sc_value = SC[i,j] and gene_sim_val = gene_sim[i,j].
  5. Filter to sc_value > 0 strictly (expect 1337 pairs). Fail fast if the count differs.
  6. Flag within_top16 = (i in Top16) and (j in Top16). Verify 117 within-top16 vs 1220 other; fail fast on mismatch.
  7. Compute Pearson r, p on the 1337 (sc, gene_sim) points and a simple linear regression (slope, intercept) with sc as predictor.

Implementation base: write a single script generated_code.py; no other repository script is required.

Outputs

  • figure.png and figure.pdf: scatter with x=SC strength, y=gene-expression Spearman similarity.
  • Non-Top16 pairs plotted first in gray #7B8794 (size 12, alpha 0.35); Top16-within pairs overlaid in red #C23B22 (size 22, alpha 0.85).
  • Black linear-fit line (lw=1.5) drawn over x ∈ [min sc among the 1337 pairs, 1].
  • Upper-left annotation: Pearson r=<r:.3f>, p=<p:.3g>\nn=1337 pairs (SC>0)\nred = Top16-within (n=117).
  • X label Structural connectivity strength; Y label Gene-expression Spearman similarity; title F1 SC vs gene-expression similarity (SC>0). Remove top and right spines; legend distinguishing gray (other) and red (Top16-within).
  • statistics.json: pearson_r, pearson_p, slope, intercept, n_total (=1337), n_top16_within (=117), n_other (=1220), mean_gene_sim_top16_within, mean_gene_sim_other, warnings (empty if all count checks pass).
  • analysis3_edge_gene_similarity_vs_fc_individuality.csv: 1337 rows with columns region_i, region_j, acro_i, acro_j, sc_value, gene_sim, within_top16.

Assumptions and Warnings

  • Gene-expression axis order is (gene, region) with the region axis aligned to the 70-atlas used by SC and the edge CSV (assumption flagged in dataset metadata).
  • Population std (ddof=0) used for gene z-scoring, matching the prompt; Spearman zero-variance rows yield NaN and are not expected here.
  • Edge-CSV deduplication assumes each unordered (i,j) with i<j appears repeatedly across hemispheric/edge variants; aggregation is by mean of numeric fields with first-row acronyms retained.
sessions.summary: SC strength and gene-expression similarity are positively correlated across all 1337 SC>0 region pairs (Pearson r=0.404, p≈1.07e-53), and Top16-within pairs occupy the upper part of this relationship with a substantially higher mean gene similarity (~0.088 vs ~0.011), suggesting the Top16 forms a structurally and transcriptomically more coherent subnetwork.

sessions.plan_html:
Goal

Compare gene-expression Spearman similarity between "Top16-within" edges (both endpoints in the fixed Top16 region set) and "Non-within" edges, restricted to region pairs with SC>0, using a raincloud visualization plus two-sided Mann–Whitney U and Kolmogorov–Smirnov tests. Report descriptive statistics, effect size (rank-biserial), and the two test statistics with p-values.

Inputs

Base directory: ~/data/zebrafish/

  • Files/gene_expression.npy — float64 array, shape (290 genes, 70 regions).
  • Files/SC_matrix_undirected_terminals_expanded.npy — float64 array, shape (70, 70), symmetric structural connectivity.
  • Atlas/acronyms.txt — 70 region acronyms in row order matching the matrices.

Region set (0-based indices):

  • Fixed Top16: [60,51,41,62,32,61,58,57,45,43,39,42,64,46,26,55].
  • Excluded regions: [10,17,34,37,44,49,50,63,66,67,68,69] → 58 kept regions.

Method

  1. Gene similarity matrix. Load gene_expression.npy (290×70). Z-score each gene across the 70 regions (axis of length 70, ddof=0). Compute scipy.stats.spearmanr across the 70 region-columns to obtain a 70×70 gene_sim matrix.
  2. Pair set. Enumerate all unordered pairs (i<j) among the 58 kept regions → 1653 pairs. Filter to pairs with SC[i,j] > 0 from the undirected expanded SC matrix. Fail fast if the SC>0 count is not 1337.
  3. Grouping. For each retained pair: within if both endpoints ∈ Top16 (expected n=117); otherwise non_within (expected n=1220). Fail fast if counts deviate.
  4. Tests.
  • scipy.stats.mannwhitneyu(within, non_within, alternative='two-sided') → U, p_mwu; effect size r = 1 - 2*U/(n_within*n_non_within) (labelled "Cliff's δ / rank-biserial" as in the prompt).
  • scipy.stats.ks_2samp(within, non_within, alternative='two-sided') → D, p_ks.
  • Descriptives per group: n, mean, median, std (population), min, max.
  1. Plot (raincloud). Two groups at x=1 (within) and x=2 (non_within):
  • Half-violin via gaussian_kde — left-facing at x=1, right-facing at x=2; fills #C23B22 α=0.4 (within) and #7B8794 α=0.4 (non_within).
  • Boxplot offset ~0.15 from violin, patch_artist=True, showfliers=False, widths=0.15, dark median line.
  • Jitter scatter on the opposite side (offset ~0.15 from center), np.random.normal(offset, 0.03, n); within red #C23B22 size 12 α 0.6, non_within gray #444444 size 8 α 0.35.
  • Significance bracket above with stars ( p<0.001, p<0.01, p<0.05, else p=<value:.3f>) based on MWU p.
  • X ticks: Top16-within\nn=117, Non-within\nn=1220. Y label: Gene-expression Spearman similarity. Title: F2 Gene similarity: Top16 vs Non-within (SC>0). Remove top/right spines. Legend for the two groups.
  • Upper-right text: MWU p=<p_mwu:.3g>\nKS D=<D:.3f>, p=<p_ks:.3g>\nCliff's δ=<r:.3f>.

Set a fixed RNG seed for jitter reproducibility.

Outputs

  • generated_code.py — self-contained script performing the above.
  • figure.png and figure.pdf — the raincloud figure described in Method.
  • statistics.json — keys: n_pairs_total (1337), per-group block (within, non_within) with {n, mean, median, std, min, max}; mwu {U, p, rank_biserial_r}; ks {D, p}; top16_indices, excluded_indices, kept_n (58); optional warnings list.
  • gene_similarity_top16_vs_non_within_sc_pos.csv — 1337 rows with columns region_i, region_j, acro_i, acro_j, sc_value, gene_sim, group (group ∈ {within, non_within}; region_i < region_j).

Assumptions and Warnings

  • Prompt labels the effect size "Cliff's δ" but defines it as the MWU rank-biserial r = 1 - 2U/(n1·n2); the plan uses that exact formula and reports it under the printed label from the prompt.
  • Gene-expression axis order (290 genes, 70 regions) is taken as given; regions are aligned with SC and acronyms row-wise.
  • The recipe (GSEA_FalsePositives) is unrelated to this raincloud/MWU/KS comparison and is not used for implementation.

caveats: Reported effect labeled as Cliff's δ in figure but computed as rank-biserial r (1-2U/n1n2); numerically equivalent for MWU.

sessions.summary: Among SC>0 region pairs, gene-expression Spearman similarity is significantly higher for Top16-within pairs (n=117, median ≈0.055) than for Non-within pairs (n=1220, median ≈-0.030), with small but consistent effect size (MWU p=0.0099, KS D=0.144 p=0.021, rank-biserial ≈-0.144).
